key.slate_infohud.toggle: Show or hide the info overlay
key.slate_infohud.toggle.tip: Switches the info overlay on and off while playing. Not bound until you give it a key.
key.slate_infohud.mode.tip: Switches the info overlay between its full and its compact size. Not bound until you give it a key.
Laid out by the game itself
slate.slot.style_only.slate.minecraft.de: Slate's look: the two columns on plates, sections with headings, values in line, the charts in frames. Every line stays as the game and other mods wrote it.
The game's own debug screen, untouched.
slate_infohud.vram.unknown: Your graphics driver does not say how much video memory is in use (Intel's and Apple's do not), so the overlay leaves that bar out rather than show a guess.
slate_infohud.vram.unknown.total: Your graphics driver says how much video memory is free but not how much there is, so the overlay leaves that bar out rather than show a guess.
slate_infohud.settings.group.overlay.abo: A small panel on the HUD with what you would open the debug screen (F3) for, and how the game is running. It hides with the HUD (F1) and while the debug screen is open, and stands clear of the chat, the boss bars, the effects, a minimap, party frames and the quest tracker.
slate_infohud.settings.group.place.about: On a server that asks for reduced debug information the position, the facing, the biome, the light and the day are withheld here as they are on the debug screen.
slate_infohud.settings.group.game.page: Info overlay: how the game runs
slate_infohud.settings.group.game.about: Read a few times a second, never every frame: the overlay itself costs next to nothing.
slate_infohud.settings.enabled.tip: Shows the overlay while you play. You can also give it a key (Controls, under Slate), which switches it on and off.
slate_infohud.settings.mode.tip: Full is a short stack of cards with every line that is switched on. Compact is a row of chips: the position, the biome, the frame rate, the latency and the two bars, small.
slate_infohud.settings.corner.tip: The corner of the screen the overlay stands in. Where something else is already there (a minimap, the effects, the chat), it stands beside or under it.
slate_infohud.settings.scale.tip: How large the overlay is against the rest of the GUI. It is drawn at the nearest whole number of screen pixels, so its text stays sharp. At 75%% and under it also gets smaller by itself where it would take more than two fifths of the window's height.
slate_infohud.settings.opacity.tip: How solid the cards and chips are. At 0 there are none and the text stands on the world with a shadow.
slate_infohud.settings.position.tip: The block you stand in: x, y, z.
slate_infohud.settings.chunk.tip: A second line under the position: the chunk you are in, and where in it you stand. Full size only.
slate_infohud.settings.facing.tip: The compass point you look towards and the axis that is: North is -Z, East is +X.
slate_infohud.settings.biome.tip: The biome you stand in, by its name.
slate_infohud.settings.dimension.tip: The dimension's name, while it is not the Overworld.
slate_infohud.settings.light.tip: The light where you stand: from blocks (what decides whether monsters spawn) and from the sky. Full size only.
slate_infohud.settings.time.tip: The number of the day and the time of day as a clock. Full size only.
slate_infohud.settings.speed.tip: How fast you move, shown only while you are faster than a sprint: riding, flying, in a boat on ice. Full size only.
slate_infohud.settings.fps.tip: Frames a second as a steady mean over the last second. Full size adds the 1%% low: the frame rate of the slowest hundredth of the last ten seconds' frames, which is what a stutter feels like.
slate_infohud.settings.graph.tip: A small live graph under the frame rate: the slowest frame of every tenth of a second, the last ten seconds of them, with the frame time of the moment beside it. A stutter shows as a spike. Full size only.
slate_infohud.settings.latency.tip: On a server: the round trip to it in milliseconds, asked once a second the way the game's own network chart asks. In a world of your own: how long the game's server takes for a tick (it falls behind above 50 ms).
slate_infohud.settings.memory.tip: The game's memory: in use, of the most it may take. The paler part of the bar is what Java has taken from the system so far; full size also says how fast the game allocates, where there is room beside the numbers. The bar turns amber and red as memory runs short.
slate_infohud.settings.videoMemory.tip: The graphics card's memory in use, of what it has, for everything on the card (the game, the desktop, other programs). Shown where the graphics driver says: NVIDIA's does, AMD's does, Intel's does not.
